name: Mississippi Civil Rights Museum
unique: A state museum that tells the movement county by county, with the names of the dead, a burned church bell and the story of Freedom Summer.
buzz: One of the best civil rights museums in the country, and the scale of the local detail is what makes it. Pair it with the adjacent history museum.

name: Natchez Trace Parkway
unique: A 444-mile two lane road with no trucks and no billboards, following a pre Columbian trail through cypress bottoms, Indian mounds and 19th century inns.
buzz: Drivers call it the most relaxing road in America; cyclists do it in a week. Gas up before you enter, services are sparse.

name: B.B. King Museum
unique: Built in the cotton gin where King worked, it tells the Delta blues story through his guitars, his tour bus and the sharecropping system that produced him.
buzz: The integration of the cotton gin building is beautifully done; staff are generous with stories. A serious museum in a small town.

name: Delta Blues Museum
unique: A museum in a former railroad depot with Muddy Waters' cabin, guitars, photographs and the story of the Delta blues.
buzz: The cabin and the instruments are the highlights, and Clarksdale itself is the experience. Go to a juke joint after.

name: Ground Zero Blues Club
customer: Music fans, young adults, road trippers
unique: A juke joint co-owned by Morgan Freeman where the walls are covered in signatures, the menu is fried everything and the blues are loud and local.
buzz: The music is the real thing; food is decent and service is slow by design. Go on a Friday and stay for the second set.

name: Walter Anderson Museum
unique: The murals of a reclusive naturalist who rowed to a barrier island alone for weeks, painted every bird and crab he saw, and decorated his cottage floor to ceiling.
buzz: Visitors call it a revelation; the community center murals are the reason to come. Small, cheap and quietly profound.

name: Longwood
unique: The largest octagonal house in the country, unfinished since the Civil War, with its original crates and tools still inside.
buzz: The unfinished interior is the fascinating part, and the tour explains why construction stopped. Book ahead in pilgrimage season.

name: Melrose
unique: A Greek Revival mansion in the Natchez National Historical Park, with original furniture and the story of the enslaved people who ran the estate.
buzz: The ranger tours are excellent and the slave quarters exhibit is part of the visit. Less flashy than the private houses and more honest.

name: Rowan Oak
unique: William Faulkner's home, preserved with his books, his outline of A Fable on the wall and the grounds he walked.
buzz: Pilgrimage for readers, and the self guided tour lets you linger. The cedar grove is quiet.

name: Vicksburg National Military Park
unique: Sixteen miles of preserved siege lines, 1,300 monuments and the ironclad USS Cairo, pulled from the Yazoo River a century after it sank.
buzz: The driving loop is excellent and the Cairo is the highlight; the terrain explains the campaign better than any book. Quiet and sobering.

name: African American Military History Museum
unique: A museum in a 1942 USO building telling the stories of Black soldiers from the Revolution to today, with uniforms, medals and oral histories.
buzz: Personal and well curated, and free. The local soldiers' stories are the strongest part.

name: GRAMMY Museum Mississippi
unique: A museum of recorded music with instruments, stage clothes and interactive mixing stations, focused on Mississippi's outsize role in American music.
buzz: The interactive studios are fun for kids and the artifacts are serious. A surprise for a small Delta town.

name: Oxford Square
unique: A courthouse square of bookshops, bars, boutiques and restaurants, with the university a few blocks away and game day crowds that fill it.
buzz: The square is the town's living room, busy on weekends and game days. The independent bookstore is the local anchor.

name: The Shed BBQ
unique: A barbecue joint built from salvaged shacks and junk, with picnic tables under the trees, a stage for live blues and ribs that win competitions.
buzz: The atmosphere is half the meal and the ribs are legitimately good; live music on weekends. A Gulf Coast institution.

name: Gulf Islands National Seashore
unique: Barrier islands with white sand and Civil War forts, reachable by ferry, with campgrounds on a spit of land you can walk at low tide.
buzz: The beaches are emptier than Florida's and the forts are a bonus; the ferry to Ship Island is the best day. Summer heat and storms.

name: Dockery Farms
unique: The cotton plantation where Charley Patton and Howlin' Wolf worked, called the birthplace of the blues, with the gin and the commissary still standing.
buzz: Blues pilgrims come from other countries and the site is quiet and unmarked; the fields and the old buildings are the whole visit.

name: Mississippi Museum of Art
unique: A state art museum with a strong collection of Mississippi and Southern artists, photography and a sculpture garden.
buzz: The Southern art is the reason, and the museum is quiet and well organized. Free on some days.

name: Old Court House Museum
unique: A 1858 courthouse on a hill with a museum of the siege, Confederate and Union relics, and a view over the Mississippi.
buzz: The collection is old fashioned and dense, and the view from the hill is the best in town. Pair it with the military park.

name: Beauvoir
unique: Jefferson Davis's last home and presidential library, with the house, the Confederate cemetery and the grounds on the Gulf.
buzz: The house and the library are the visit, and the view of the Gulf is a bonus. The history is presented uncritically, so bring your own context.

name: Choctaw Indian Fair
unique: A Choctaw fair with stickball games, tribal dances, crafts and a world championship stickball tournament, on the reservation in central Mississippi.
buzz: The stickball is the reason to come and it is fast and physical; the fair is one of the oldest Native American gatherings in the country.

name: Corinth Civil War Interpretive Center
unique: A center on the 1862 battle and the occupation of Corinth, with a water sculpture that traces the war and the earthworks outside.
buzz: The sculpture and the ranger talks are the reasons to stop; the town also has the old depot and the Contraband Camp site.

name: Dentzel Carousel
unique: A 1909 Dentzel menagerie carousel with hand carved animals, still running in a pavilion in Highland Park.
buzz: The animals are beautiful and the ride costs a dollar. A genuine piece of Americana.

name: Elvis Presley Birthplace
unique: The two-room shotgun house where Elvis was born, preserved on its original lot with the Assembly of God church he sang in moved next door.
buzz: Modest and moving, especially the church; less spectacle than Graceland and better for it. The gift shop is exactly what you'd expect.

name: Fondren
unique: A walkable neighborhood of bungalows, coffee shops, bars, a brewery and a cinema, the social center of young Jackson.
buzz: The district is compact and busy on weekends, with a good brunch scene. Park once and walk.

name: Natchez Trace Visitor Center
unique: The headquarters of the Natchez Trace Parkway, with a museum on the old trace, a film and the start of the 444 mile drive.
buzz: The film and the exhibits explain why the trace exists, and the parkway is the real attraction. Free.

name: Shearwater Pottery
unique: A family pottery studio founded by the Anderson family, with a showroom of glazed pots and tiles made on site.
buzz: The pottery is beautiful and the prices are fair for handmade work. Pair it with the Walter Anderson Museum.

name: Square Books
unique: A bookstore on the Oxford square with a balcony over the courthouse, three floors of books and a writer's room upstairs.
buzz: Writers treat it as a pilgrimage and the readings are the local event; the balcony is the place to sit with a coffee.

name: Bay St. Louis Old Town
unique: A Gulf coast town of restored cottages and live oaks on the bay, with a beach, a small arts district and a rebuilt main street after Katrina.
buzz: The town is quieter than the casinos and the beach is free; the old town walk and the seafood are the reasons to stop.

name: Biloxi Lighthouse
unique: A 1848 lighthouse standing in the middle of a highway, with a climb to the top and a view of the beach and the bay.
buzz: The setting in the median is strange and the climb is short. A quick photo stop.

name: Cotton District
unique: A neighborhood of restored mill cottages, bars and restaurants next to the Mississippi State campus, rebuilt after a tornado.
buzz: The district is walkable and busy on game weekends. Good for a casual dinner.

name: Tennessee Williams Home
unique: The boyhood home of the playwright, with family furniture, photographs and the bedroom where he wrote his first stories.
buzz: Small and personal, best for theater people. The Columbus historic district around it is worth a walk.

name: Tunica RiverPark
unique: A river museum and boardwalk on the Mississippi with aquariums of river fish, a replica of a 19th century riverboat and a nature trail.
buzz: The riverboat and the boardwalk are the family stops and the river is right there; the casinos across the road are the other Tunica.

name: Mississippi Petrified Forest
unique: A eroded gully full of 36-million year old petrified logs, with a small museum and a nature trail that looks like another planet.
buzz: It is small, cheap and weird in the best way; geologists love it. Worth a stop if you're already on I-55.

name: Museum of the Mississippi Delta
unique: A museum of the Delta's cotton economy, with farm equipment, a sharecropper cabin and the story of the Chinese and Italian immigrants who worked the fields.
buzz: The local history is specific and honest and the volunteers know the families; it is small and cheap.
